land.text: the Bari, Nugaal and Mudug regions of north-eastern Somalia; the page says only the northern part of Mudug is Puntland's ('the southern part of Mudug is part of Galmudug')

predecessors.note: Puntland 'is a federal member state of Somalia'; Cliopatria's Federal Republic of Somalia row (1960-2024) still draws the area as Somali land.

correction.text: the Bari, Nugaal and Mudug regions of north-eastern Somalia; the page says only the northern part of Mudug is Puntland's ('the southern part of Mudug is part of Galmudug')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). 'Established: 1 August 1998'; infobox area 212,510 km2 of land. Bari, Nugaal and Mudug resolve to about 198,000 km2 in the gazetteer (ratio 0.93): whole Mudug overshoots (the south is Galmudug's) while Sool and Sanaag, claimed but disputed, are left out and drawn as contest.

Maakhir, the short-lived quasi-state of the eastern Sanaag coast incorporated in January 2009

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'In January 2009, the short-lived quasi-state of Maakhir was officially incorporated into Puntland.' Maakhir is a region name the gazetteer lacks; the page also says Puntland created Gardafuul from Bari in 2013 and Haylaan from Sanaag, internal changes.

region.text: the Bari, Nugaal and Mudug regions of north-eastern Somalia; the page says only the northern part of Mudug is Puntland's ('the southern part of Mudug is part of Galmudug')

ledger.note: 1998 (1 August): Puntland is established. Infobox 'Established: 1 August 1998'; a constitutional conference 'was held in Garoowe in 1998 over a period of three months'; capital Garowe.

union.text: Las Anod and the Sool lands round it

region.text: Sool, Sanaag and Ayn (Cayn), the zone disputed with Somaliland

ledger.note: 1998: the dispute with Somaliland over Sool, Sanaag and Ayn begins. Puntland has been in 'territorial disputes with Somaliland over the Sool, Sanaag and Ayn regions' since 1998; the Dhulbahante were 'torn between supporting Somaliland, Puntland, or the formation of an independent entity' (Sool, Sanaag and Cayn page).

region.text: Las Anod and the Sool lands round it

ledger.note: 2007 (October): Somaliland takes Las Anod. 'In October 2007, Somaliland troops took control of the town' of Las Anod (Somaliland page, which does not name Puntland as the party that lost it); the Sanaag claim goes on, and Khatumo State was declared on 12 January 2012.

region.text: Maakhir, the short-lived quasi-state of the eastern Sanaag coast incorporated in January 2009

ledger.note: 2009 (January): Maakhir joins Puntland. 'In January 2009, the short-lived quasi-state of Maakhir was officially incorporated into Puntland.'

wars.name: Sool and Sanaag dispute with Somaliland

union.text: Las Anod and the Sool lands round it

zones.text: Sool, Sanaag and Ayn (Cayn), the zone disputed with Somaliland

wars.outcome: Somaliland took Las Anod in October 2007; the dispute over Sanaag continues and SSC-Khatumo took Las Anod from Somaliland in 2023.
wars.note: The Sool, Sanaag and Cayn page has no 1998 or 2007 dates; the Puntland page gives only 'since 1998' and does not mention Las Anod.

certainty.note: Borders with Somaliland, Galmudug and the Khatumo administration are fronts and clan lines, not surveyed; the page calls the southern half of Mudug disputed ('citation needed').

notes:
Written from three pages; the Puntland article does not mention Las Anod, Tukaraq or the 2023 Las Anod conflict, so Puntland's role there is not dated here (Sool, Sanaag and Cayn page: Khatumo captured Tukaraq from Puntland troops and Somaliland and Puntland recaptured it in a coordinated offensive on 16 June, year not given; the Federal Government acknowledged SSC-Khatumo on 19 October 2023 and Puntland on 17 July 2025 was 'refusing to recognize the Khatumo administration').
Not settled: Puntland's actual hold on Sool and eastern Sanaag between 1998 and 2007 (page silent); the northern limit of its Mudug territory; Galmudug's border; the status change of 31 March 2024, when the government 'no longer recognizes the authority of the Somali federal government' (the page's date; no land changes hands, so no event); the 2012 constitution convention (opened 15 April 2012). Counterparts: federal-republic-of-somalia (Cliopatria row), somaliland (this batch), maakhir (a quasi-state of 2007-2009 with no dossier). Gazetteer names needed: 'Maakhir' (region: eastern Sanaag coast, Badhan and Las Qoray).
